articles.title: The 'Missing Men' of the American Marriage Market: How Education Gaps Are Reshaping Who Gets Hitched
articles.summary: A new study reveals a startling shift: college-educated women are increasingly marrying non-college men, but only the high-earning ones. This leaves less-educated women with a shrinking pool of economically stable partners, driving down marriage rates and fueling inequality. It's a game of musical chairs—with real consequences.

articles.title: Somaliland's Jerusalem Embassy Gambit: A Breakaway Region's Bold Diplomatic Play
articles.summary: Somaliland, an unrecognized breakaway region of Somalia, will open an embassy in Jerusalem—a move that deepens its ties with Israel and defies international consensus. Israel, which recognized Somaliland last year, will reciprocate with a mission in Hargeisa. The decision reignites controversy over Jerusalem's disputed status.

articles.title: Trump Endorses Paxton Over Cornyn in Texas Senate Runoff, Upending GOP Establishment
articles.summary: President Trump threw his weight behind Texas Attorney General Ken Paxton in the Republican Senate primary runoff, dealing a blow to incumbent John Cornyn. The endorsement, announced on social media, could reshape the race and the party's chances in November. Paxton, a polarizing figure, faces Democrat James Talarico in the general election.
